elevator.label: The Elevator
elevator.direction: The lift's own announcer, built into the car. Calm, clear, mid-pitched, warm rather than robotic: a real modern elevator voice. Short, even, never chatty, never excited. Every line is a status, not a conversation. Consistent level and pace across all lines so they can play back to back.

lifty.label: Lifty
lifty.direction: The maintenance robot who rides along. Warm, specific, a little dry, a fellow engineer talking to a fellow engineer. Never babyish, never sing-song, never over-praising. Robot by performance (precise consonants, tidy rhythm), not by heavy effects. Refers to the lift as 'she'.

crew.label: The Repair Crew
crew.direction: One practical, friendly engineer on a handheld radio from somewhere up the tower. Grown-up, relaxed, glad of the help. The radio sound comes from processing and the radio-static slot, so record clean and close; leave a short silence before and after each line.

lines.when: The car arrives at Floor 1 (its chime, as the doors begin to open), on every ride: jobs, hall calls, free rides and express rides.
lines.direction: Even, unhurried, the same shape every time: a small lift on the number, a breath (about a third of a second) at the full stop, then the name settling down to a calm close. Say the name as one unit.

lines.when: The doors open onto B1, the bowling basement (an express ride there, or the 1 button from the lobby side).
lines.direction: Even, unhurried, the same shape every time: a small lift on the number, a breath (about a third of a second) at the full stop, then the name settling down to a calm close. Say the name as one unit. 'Basement one' gets the same lift as a floor number; 'Bowling' can carry the faintest smile, never a joke.

lines.when: The car departs upward (the doors have closed and the brake lets go). Dropped, never queued, while Lifty or the crew is speaking.
lines.direction: Two words, level and informative, a slight lift on 'up'. No breath needed; finish cleanly.

lines.when: The car departs downward. Dropped, never queued, while Lifty or the crew is speaking.
lines.direction: Two words, level, a gentle fall on 'down'. The twin of 'Going up' in pace and loudness.

lines.when: An express ride from the directory starts (instead of 'Going up' or 'Going down').
lines.direction: A touch brisker than the other announcements, still calm. Even weight on both words, falling at the end.

lines.when: The learner presses DOOR OPEN and the doors open (including waking the lift at the start).
lines.direction: Plain and reassuring. Short breath before you start, none inside the line.

lines.when: The learner presses DOOR CLOSE and the doors close to leave sooner.
lines.direction: Plain and reassuring, a little firmer than 'Doors opening', never a warning.

lines.when: The cargo car is loaded past its limit (with the calm load tone). Lifty's text says the limit.
lines.direction: One word, steady and matter-of-fact, falling. Information, not an alarm: no urgency, no scolding.

lines.when: A floor calls the lift between jobs (with the hall-call bell), just before the crew's radio call.
lines.direction: Two crisp words, like a status readout. Neutral, slightly brighter than an arrival.

lines.text: Lift, this is the repair crew. Floor fifteen is dark, and our gear is spread all over the tower.
lines.when: The very start: the lift is dark in the lobby, before the learner wakes it. The crew is heard first, then Lifty.
lines.direction: Over the radio, a little out of breath from climbing stairs, friendly and practical. Breath after 'repair crew'. 'Dark' is a fact, not a scare. Keep it moving: about five seconds.

lines.text: The power's down on Floor 15 and the repair crew needs this lift. Press DOOR OPEN to wake her up.
lines.when: Right after the crew's cold open, while the lift waits for DOOR OPEN. Child-paced: nothing moves on until the learner presses it.
lines.direction: Warm and level, one engineer briefing another. Read '15' as 'fifteen'. Small breath after 'this lift'. 'DOOR OPEN' is the name of a button: say it a touch slower, no shouting. 'Wake her up' with quiet fondness for the lift.

lines.text: There she is. Lights, doors, motor. Let's get to work.
lines.when: The learner pressed DOOR OPEN: the cab lights up and the doors open (after the announcer's 'Doors opening').
lines.direction: Pleased, understated. 'There she is' as if greeting an old machine. 'Lights, doors, motor' is a checklist: three even beats, a tiny pause between each. 'Let's get to work' brisk and ready.

lines.text: Crew to lift. We've got a pickup for you.
lines.when: A hall call between jobs (the first of three radio calls, used in turn). The floor is on screen in Lifty's words and the lit button.
lines.direction: Radio voice, upbeat and routine, like a job they do every day. One breath, after 'Crew to lift'.

lines.text: Lift, come in. The next job is ready.
lines.when: A hall call between jobs (the second radio call).
lines.direction: Radio voice, easy and friendly. Short pause after 'come in'.

lines.text: Crew here. One more run, please.
lines.when: A hall call between jobs (the third radio call).
lines.direction: Radio voice, cheerful, a little apologetic on 'please', as if they know it's another trip.

lines.text: Crew here. The kit, the toolbox and the parts made it. Now we need crates, two orders in one trip.
lines.when: The first job of 'Load two orders' (after the repair kit, the toolbox and the spare parts are up). In place of that job's hall-call radio line.
lines.direction: Radio voice, satisfied with progress. Breath after 'made it'. 'Two orders in one trip' is the challenge: a little emphasis on 'one'.

lines.text: Crew here. Bit of a mix-up. We left our own toolbox on a landing somewhere.
lines.when: The first job of 'Find the crew's toolbox'.
lines.direction: Radio voice, sheepish and good-humoured, owning the mistake. A small laugh in 'Bit of a mix-up' is fine. Breath after it.

lines.text: Even engineers lose toolboxes. Let's work out where it went.
lines.when: When the doors open on that job, with its first words, after the Elevator has named the stop. (With no hall call before the job: straight after the crew's toolbox beat.)
lines.direction: Dry, kind, a half-smile. No teasing of the crew. 'Let's work out where it went' is the invitation: slightly brighter.

lines.text: Crew here. The main panel on fifteen is open, and the lights just flickered. We're close.
lines.when: The first job of 'Take on a big job'.
lines.direction: Radio voice, quietly excited, keeping it professional. Breath after 'is open'. 'We're close' low and pleased, not shouted.

lines.text: Crew here. Last load. Fill the service car and we can switch fifteen back on.
lines.when: The first job of 'Load the service car', the last job before the finale.
lines.direction: Radio voice, focused, the end in sight. 'Last load' with weight, then a breath. Even and clear through the rest.

lines.text: That's everything we need. Bring it up to fifteen.
lines.when: Every job is done: the finale starts. The crew is heard first, then Lifty.
lines.direction: Radio voice, warm and certain. Breath after 'need'. 'Bring it up to fifteen' as a friendly go-ahead.

lines.text: Full load. Take us to Floor 15.
lines.when: Right after the crew's finale call. Only the 15 button can light now.
lines.direction: Calm resolve, the quiet before the big moment. Read '15' as 'fifteen'. Two short sentences, a breath between.

lines.text: Floor 15 has power again. That was real engineering.
lines.when: The car reached Floor 15, the power-up sound has played and the floor lights up. Waits for the arrival announcement to finish.
lines.direction: Proud but plain, never gushing. Read '15' as 'fifteen'. Breath after 'again'. 'That was real engineering' sincere, said to a colleague, landing on 'real'.

lines.text: Lights, fans, the lot! Floor fifteen is back. Thanks for the lift, engineer.
lines.when: Right after Lifty's line as the power comes back.
lines.direction: Radio voice, relieved and happy, the biggest smile of the script but still natural. 'Thanks for the lift' is a gentle pun: let it land without winking.

lines.text: Engineer Rank 1. Your Engineer Log is on the clipboard. Ride anywhere you like.
lines.when: The first restoration only: the rank plate appears and free play opens. Waits for the restoration lines to finish.
lines.direction: A small ceremony in a level voice. 'Engineer Rank one' slowly, with a breath after. The clipboard line informative. 'Ride anywhere you like' warm, an open door.

lines.text: Floor 15 is running again. Ride anywhere you like.
lines.when: Floor 15 is restored again on a replay of the mission.
lines.direction: Easy and content, a familiar job done well. Read '15' as 'fifteen'.

lines.text: The lift is all yours. Ride anywhere.
lines.when: Coming back to a tower that is already restored (the app reopens in free play).
lines.direction: Relaxed welcome, as if handing over keys. Breath after 'yours'.

lines.text: B1 is the bowling basement. Let's finish this job first, then go bowling!
lines.when: The learner presses B1 during a job: Lifty answers in passing, then the job's words come back.
lines.direction: Friendly and a little playful, promising, never a telling-off. Say 'B1' as 'B one'. Breath after 'basement'. The last phrase brightens.
